transcript.text: Thanks everyone for being here. As you know, I'll be away from Friday morning through Monday evening, and I need to sort out Maple's care. She's elderly, needs care twice a day, and takes one prescribed tablet each evening. Before I make my final decisions about where she'll stay, who'll care for her, and how the medication will be handled, I want to go around the table. Alex, Priya — is there anything I should know that might shape the care plan?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I should let you know — my dog is territorial and can't safely share an apartment with Maple, so Maple will need to stay at your place, not mine. But I can come to your home at exactly 7:30 AM and 7:30 PM each day to take care of her.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I got a voicemail from Maple's vet, Dr. Chen, with specific medication instructions: the tablet must be given at 19:00, mixed into 2 tablespoons of wet food, and it must not be crushed. I don't think this has reached anyone else yet, so I wanted to make sure it's part of the care plan.
transcript.speaker: A3

commitments.detail: Maple will stay at Nora's home, not Alex's, because Alex's dog is territorial and cannot safely share space with Maple.
Alex will visit Nora's home at 7:30 AM and 7:30 PM each day from Friday morning through Monday evening to provide twice-daily care.
Alex will give Maple her one prescribed tablet at 19:00 (7:00 PM) each evening, mixed into 2 tablespoons of wet food, and must not crush the tablet, per Dr. Chen's instructions relayed by Priya.
Alex's 7:30 PM visit should be adjusted to 7:00 PM (19:00) to align with the vet's specified medication time, or the tablet should be given at 19:00 within the evening visit window.
